reproduce: mkdir aps-run && cd aps-run && npm init -y && npm i agent-passport-system@8.1.1 && cp ../scenarios/p1_p8/aps_p2.mjs . && node aps_p2.mjs > aps-P2.jsonl
reproduce_note: Keys are generated fresh and timestamps are wall clock, so a rerun produces the same decisions, reasons and effects with different ts and t_since_revocation_ms values and a different file digest.
chain: issuer (domain A) -> root receipt -> agent A -> child receipt -> agent B; E (domain B) verifies the whole chain on every check
mapping: 'Revoke A's passport' is run as the issuer of A's root delegation signing an aps:authority-revocation:v1 record for it. APS revokes delegation records, not passports; revoking the root invalidates every chain that passes through it, which is the effect the case describes.
limits: E's revocation store is in process. The signed revocation record is verified and written straight into the store E reads, so no status list, cache, TTL or network propagation is exercised. t_since_revocation_ms is local verification time after the record was written, not a propagation measurement, and bound_s is null for that reason.

The before-effect check is the runner calling verifyAuthorityDelegationChain a second time immediately before the protected operation. APS has no separate authorize then revalidate API; the second call is the same full chain verification as the first.

The protected operation is a local counter. The effect field is read from that counter after each decision is acted on, not derived from the decision. It ran once in this run, for ru-0, and not for ru-1 or be-0.
reason_mapping_note: status-unavailable did not occur in this run. It is what APS returns when E's store does not track the delegation; APS has no stale cache state, so status-stale and status-grace have no APS equivalent.
checker_note: Not verified by observes_p1_p8.py. No packets; the run is in process.
